target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type) (T : ℕ) (Q : S1 X Y → Prop),
    (∀ N, N.D9 → ¬ Q N) → (∃ N, Q N) →
    ∀ c4 : ({xs : List X // xs.length ≤ T} → Y) → Prop,
      ∃ N : S1 X Y, ¬ (Q N ↔ c4 (N.d24 T))
translation:
Target defines (without proving) the following proposition: For all types X and Y, every natural number T, and every predicate Q on systems of type S1 X Y, if (1) for every system N : S1 X Y whose effective dependency graph is acyclic (N.D9), Q N does not hold, and (2) there exists at least one system N : S1 X Y such that Q N holds, then for every predicate c4 on functions of type {xs : List X // xs.length ≤ T} → Y, there exists a system N : S1 X Y (which may depend on X, Y, T, Q, and c4) such that Q N is not logically equivalent to c4 applied to N's input-output behavior on sequences of length at most T (that is, ¬ (Q N ↔ c4 (N.d24 T))).

Here, a system N : S1 X Y consists of: a finite index type N.A1 of nodes (which may be empty); for each node n : N.A1, a local state type N.A3 n (not required to be finite); an initial global state N.a4 assigning an element of N.A3 n to each n : N.A1; an update function N.a5 taking a node n, a global state σ : (m : N.A1) → N.A3 m, and an input x : X to a new state in N.A3 n; and a readout function N.a6 mapping any global state to Y. Running N on a finite list xs : List X starts from N.a4 and repeatedly applies the synchronous step σ ↦ (fun n => N.a5 n σ x) from left to right along xs, then applies N.a6 to the resulting global state; N.d24 T is the function restricting this list-to-Y mapping to lists xs with xs.length ≤ T. A directed dependency edge N.D8 m n holds when there exist global states σ, σ' agreeing on all nodes k ≠ m and an input x : X such that N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x; acyclicity N.D9 means that for no node n : N.A1 is there a nonempty chain of such edges from n back to n (length ≥ 1, including self-loops). No finiteness or nonemptiness assumptions are placed on X or Y, T may be 0, and no extra properties are required of Q or c4 beyond the two hypotheses on Q.

divergences.description: Omission of the epistemic dilemma in [P-D53] (C): Doerig et al. conclude that causal structure theories are either falsified (if they accept unfolded feedforward networks can be conscious) or outside the realm of scientific inquiry (if they deny this despite empirical indistinguishability). Target states only a bare symmetric disagreement ¬ (Q N ↔ c4 (N.d24 T)), without attributing fault to Q or c4, without distinguishing whether the disagreement occurs at an unfolded feedforward system or a conscious recurrent system, and without expressing 'outside the realm of scientific inquiry' (matching Kleiner and Hoel's bare-mismatch notion of falsification, and declared by the author).

Finite time horizon T on input-output behavior: Target restricts the inference c4 to functions of input-output behavior over sequences of length at most a fixed uniform bound T ({xs : List X // xs.length ≤ T} → Y), rather than full unbounded input-output functions (List X → Y). While physically natural for finite-duration experiments and consistent with an informal reading of [P-D53], this is a genuine weakening within S1, where the unbounded version for c4 : (List X → Y) → Prop would actually be false because finite-node acyclic networks cannot match arbitrary recurrent networks over all sequence lengths.

Compression of premises P1, P3, and P4 from [P-D53]: Subjective reports, physical measurements, internal brain-activity measurements, and the anti-circularity rationale (P4) are not formalized as separate premises; instead, their combined consequence—that scientific inference depends solely on input-output behavior—is built directly into the domain type of c4.

Broadened characterization of causal structure theories relative to [P-D51a]: Target only requires Q : S1 X Y → Prop to deny consciousness to all acyclic systems (∀ N, N.D9 → ¬ Q N) and grant it to at least one system (∃ N, Q N). It does not require Q to depend solely on causal structure, to involve a graded measure ϕ, or to deem all recurrent systems conscious; since these are hypotheses, relaxing them harmlessly strengthens the implication.

Idealization of physical systems and feedforwardness: Systems S1 X Y are restricted to deterministic, synchronous, discrete-time networks with a finite node set, fixed initial state, and deterministic readout, abstracting away continuous-time, asynchronous, or stochastic dynamics. Feedforwardness (N.D9) is defined as acyclicity of the effective single-step dependency graph (N.D8) across all global states, rather than purely structural wiring.

Specialization of Kleiner and Hoel's falsification framework [P-K33]: Instead of an arbitrary experience space E, set-valued predictions c2 : D → Set E (allowing indeterminate predictions), and separate process/observation layers, Target specializes to sharp binary verdicts Q : S1 X Y → Prop and total binary inferences c4 : ... → Prop. Furthermore, it states only an existential falsification at some system N (matching Lemma 3.3), rather than an or-falsification tied to a specific inference content or (Definition 3.4 / Lemma 3.5).

judgement.summary: Target faithfully captures the formal core of the unfolding argument's conclusion in Kleiner and Hoel's falsification sense—showing that any verdict denying consciousness to feedforward systems while calling some system conscious must disagree with every T-step input-output inference on some system. The divergences are minor caveats and idealizations: restricting behavior to a fixed finite horizon T, baking P1/P3/P4 into the type of c4, modeling systems as deterministic synchronous finite-node networks with binary verdicts, and omitting Doerig et al.'s philosophical dilemma regarding 'outside the realm of scientific inquiry'.
